## Fresh exact independent final assessment

## Complete interaction assessment

Source-to-package: canonical route uses Codex/Claude forms matched by the narrow portability recognizer. Supported manifests, independent raw-resource inventory, generated frontmatter checks and ordinary/staged archives preserve both targets' complete skills. The removal of obsolete mirror production transfers protection to existing real package checks. Bounded output preflight prevents source/runtime overlap, nested symlink, shared-inode and special-file writes while allowing valid generated package prefixes; it is not misrepresented as a concurrent generation transaction.

Package-to-install: actual candidate generation overlays current skills/scripts/templates/CLI, creates fresh metadata/index, packs the CLI and performs real two-target smoke. CLI verifies trusted metadata and selected archive before candidate preflight. Default conflict semantics include identical/empty units; force performs complete selected replacement via anchored parents, outside-discovery original retention and no-clobber publication. Partial/retry/changed-ancestor safeguards compose through the public command. State is neither read nor written and does not authorize installation; OpenCode/removed flags reject before acquisition. Linux capability limits remain explicit.

Release and history: current profiles/execution/public inventory and newly generated verification receipts describe Codex/Claude only. Receipt proof reads the actual generated release-verification.json after actual smoke. Historical archive/metadata, timing/publication and immutable rollback readers preserve original three-target facts without reopening current production/install. New current archives are validated against fresh generated identity rather than old static v0.5.1 hashes; real packed candidate proof retains the current trust chain.

Retirement and validation: exact15 sources/ADRs relinquish only mapped authorities; mixed sections/current links point to Distribution while original historical files and Follow-on evidence stay unchanged. Deleted mirror commands are absent from executable catalogs but historical IDs remain scoped. Selected lifecycle validation filters only changed, proven absent lifecycle artifacts after all contributors, preserving present/symlink/unproven and PR revision-bound checks. Broad smoke now invokes the same existing current manifest validator, not the rejecting legacy adapter. Its auto-discovery does not activate unrelated historical descendants, while reserved, explicit, symlink/indeterminate and current-manifest inputs still validate. These paths now agree instead of selected CI passing while broad CI invokes a retired reader.

## Checklist

1. Spec alignment: pass. Combined Distribution, exact old-source retirement, OpenCode withdrawal, stale mirror removal and final conflict/force/no-state behavior all remain delivered. No original goal is omitted or weakened by CI repair.
2. Test coverage: pass. Real helper/public/archives/packed/release/reader/selector/prose checks retain relevant positive and negative boundaries. Current broad validator was actually executed; wrapper-specific assertions alone are not used as record-validity proof. Corrected receipt is checked in actual candidate output.
3. Edge cases: pass within scoped contracts. Full destination conflicts, unsafe/racing parents, partial multi-unit install, retained old-handle writes, output aliases/hardlinks/FIFO, historical target populations, plan-index deletion composition, historical nonactivation and reserved/explicit non-suppression have direct evidence. No unsupported platform or external concurrency guarantee is implied.
4. Error handling: pass. Failures remain observable and truthful. Both broad aggregate failures stay failures in evidence; static assertion correction is freshly run. Current validation fails closed on malformed/unsupported stores, and installation/generation never treat force or missing state as permission to bypass safety.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass. Distribution/Skill/Release/System/Workflow/CLI/Test/Review ownership remains coherent. The CI wrapper chooses exact current manifests but does not parse schemas or emulate legacy support. The new truthful receipt label changes no schema or publication authority.
6. Compatibility: pass for approved breaking scope and preserved history. Current two-target behavior and guidance match; old release bytes/IDs retain meaning. Conditional governance transfer and FU-013 await successful Verify. Historical discovery is distinct from explicit validation, and the latter keeps rejecting unsupported inputs.
7. Security/privacy: pass. Trust precedes mutation; containment, normalized hashes/counts, no-clobber and private retention remain. CI repair adds no permissions, external trigger, parser fallback, credential exposure or new storage service. Residual platform/proof limits are explicit.
8. Derived artifact currency: pass for final Code Review. Current archive/metadata/packed execution and generated receipts are freshly exercised. No stale cloned canonical skills or removed script survives candidate fixture overlay. Installed local skill bodies remain untouched; no public release success is claimed.
9. Unrelated changes: pass. Additional CI/selector/receipt fixes are real consumers of the selected retirement/current-record boundaries. Removed tests cover expressly withdrawn semantics or stale literal expectations, while shared negative protection remains. No unrelated follow-up, validator framework, cache or dependency is added.
10. Validation evidence: pass with explicit composed results. Evidence supports all implementation obligations and the affected later corrections; it does not claim a fictional aggregate broad exit0. Distinct Verify must still adjudicate final freshness, blocker disposition, preserved limitations and closeout rather than importing this Code Review as successful Verify.
